A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same hand-object diffusion work, renamed from MGD to JHOD. Their main text, equations, tables, figures and appendices are readable and support comparison, including matching relocated material.

before.justification: v1 reports original grasp-generation experiments, user ratings, training-data and scheduler ablations, and qualitative demonstrations in its appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results and adds an ARCTIC baseline comparison, contact visualizations and qualitative comparisons with GrabNet.

M1.justification: The architecture, losses and sampling procedures match after renaming MGD to JHOD. However, v2 Equation (9) adds object-latent conditioning to the hand corruption kernel without explaining its relationship to unchanged Equation (3). Whether this represents an actual procedural change or a revision of the mathematical description is unclear.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same dataset resources and conditional, unconditional and grasp-guided image-generation tasks. ARCTIC already appears in v1's evaluation and Table 2; adding its baseline comparison does not introduce a dataset. The new bottle and contact analyses remain within existing coverage.

E2.justification: v2 adds GrabNet-Refine to the ARCTIC comparison, where v1 reported only proposed-method training-data ablations. Appendix F also adds a paired qualitative comparison with GrabNet. Existing OakInk and self-generated-object comparator sets remain unchanged; DexDiffuser is discussed but not evaluated.

E3.justification: New Appendix E specifies contact visualization using a 0.005-meter mesh-face distance threshold and three viewpoints. Appendix F specifies random sampling of unseen OakInk bottles without cherry-picking. The existing quantitative metrics and 15-participant user-study procedure are retained.

E4.justification: Appendices E–F add contact-area inspection and case-by-case comparisons of penetration and missing contact against GrabNet. These extend the qualitative diagnostic evidence. The training-data and asynchronous-scheduler ablations in Tables 2–4, and the existing failure-case analysis, are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed counts, repeated-training uncertainty, confidence intervals or significance tests. The user-score averaging procedure and rough estimate that failures constitute less than 10% of samples are unchanged.

E6.justification: v2 Table 1 newly reports GrabNet-Refine's ARCTIC results, including FID 37.23 and penetration depth 1.22. JHOD's ARCTIC values already appeared in v1 Table 2; matched original table scores remain unchanged. Figures 11–12 add qualitative outcomes, while Figure 3 drops the frying-pan examples.

T1.justification: Equation (9) revises the written hand-corruption kernel from conditioning only on the previous hand latent to conditioning on both previous hand and object latents. This changes the formal dependency specification, although its procedural implications are unexplained. Other mathematics is retained apart from notation and numbering.

C1.justification: v2 removes v1's explicit introductory claim to be first to use asynchronous schedulers to solve training instability from unpaired heterogeneous annotations. The central claims of joint and conditional generation, heterogeneous-data training and generalization to unseen objects remain.

C2.justification: Section 4.3 replaces v1's assertion that unconditional generation is on par with object-conditioned GrabNet with a comparison to ARCTIC generation. Appendix F qualifies its visual-superiority conclusion by acknowledging residual JHOD penetration. The earlier general failure explanations and physical-validity limitations remain.

D1.justification: v2 newly specifies resampling 2048 points whenever an object is drawn, including inference, three-view rendering for evaluation, and matched training curricula in the scheduler ablation. These disclosures do not establish changed experiments. Conversely, v1's promised code-and-weights repository address disappears without a replacement.

R1.justification: v2 adds Chan and Gao's 2022 works as precedents for rendered-image evaluation and cites DexDiffuser. A new baseline discussion explains comparison difficulties involving G-HOP's conditioning and reconstruction protocol and robotic-hand methods such as UGG and DexDiffuser. The broader research positioning remains similar.

P1.justification: The abstract, substantial introductory passages, experimental discussion and conclusion are rewritten. The paper and method are renamed, explanations are expanded, a baseline-selection passage is added, and qualitative material is reorganized between the main text and appendices. This is extensive editorial revision despite substantial scientific continuity.

P2.justification: The document changes from a two-column format to a single-column journal layout. Figures 3–4 move into the main text, Figure 3's sample grid is reduced, Table 1 gains an ARCTIC block, and Figures 11–12 add contact and baseline-comparison displays. Most earlier visual content is retained.

improvement.justification: The added ARCTIC baseline comparison and contact and qualitative analyses modestly strengthen the evidence for generalization and grasp quality. Newly documented sampling and rendering details also improve assessability. The gain is limited because matched numerical results and ablations remain unchanged, while removal of the code-release pointer and the unexplained Equation (9) revision weaken reproducibility and methodological clarity.
